extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH/NINDS extramural grant applications (principal investigators, senior/key personnel, and administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on additional application components applicants must include or consider when preparing NIH (NINDS) grant submissions, describing what to include, formatting limits, and how reviewers will use each element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a succinct summary of the project that both a scientist and a lay person can understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Specific Aims as a template—shorten and simplify the language. In the first sentence, state the significance of your research to the field and relevance to NIND's mission: to better understand, treat, and prevent infectious, immunologic, and allergic diseases. Next state the hypothesis and the innovative potential of your research. Then list and briefly describe the Specific Aims and long-term objectives. Include appropriate keywords (e.g., immunotherapy, genetic risk factors). Do not include graphics or citations. Define or omit abbreviations. Omit confidential or proprietary information. Note: Abstract and Narrative are publicly posted in RePORTER and read by all peer reviewers and NIH staff who use them for assignment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix — allowable materials
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH limits the information you may put in an Appendix; follow NOFO-specific guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable Appendix materials are limited to: blank data collection forms, blank survey/questionnaire forms (or screenshots), simple lists of interview questions, blank informed consent/assent forms, and other items only if specified in the NOFO. Do not use the Appendix to bypass Research Plan page limits. Applications with unallowable Appendix materials will be withdrawn and not reviewed. Submit Appendix via the Appendix attachment of the PHS 398 Research Plan form; contact the Scientific Review Officer if you cannot submit electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment Request Form (PHS Assignment Request)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional form to suggest assignment preferences and reviewer expertise to NIH CSR’s Division of Receipt and Referral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains four sections for receiving suggestions from applicants; DRR reviews but is not required to follow suggestions. Only NIH staff involved in assignment and review have access. Use this form to recommend primary IC assignment (choose IC whose mission aligns with your research), suggest study section assignment (check NOFO 'Section V' and use CSR Assisted Referral Tool), and list expertise needed to review your application. NIH’s Matchmaker and contacting a NINDS Program Officer may help. Making assignment suggestions can be helpful if you can write for a specific study section/audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion of IC assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend the Institute/Center whose mission most closely aligns with your proposed research when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIH’s Matchmaker if unsure and consider reaching out to a NINDS Program Officer. For parent funding opportunities or those with multiple participating ICs, recommending an IC can guide assignment decisions (see NOFO 'Components of Participating Organizations').

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section assignment guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether applications will be reviewed by CSR or an IC-convened panel and suggest appropriate study sections if helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review 'Section V' of the NOFO and 'Peer Review Contact(s)' in 'Section VII' for where your application will be reviewed. If CSR review applies, the CSR Assisted Referral Tool can indicate suitable standing study sections. NINDS program staff can also provide input. Writing toward a specific study section can be beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuals who should not review (exclusion requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting exclusion of a potential reviewer, provide specific reasons why they could not provide a fair and impartial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH review staff assess conflicts of interest; a scientific competitor does not necessarily constitute a conflict. Provide specific details—actions or observations—that suggest inability to be impartial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas of expertise needed to review your application
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the disciplines and expertise needed to evaluate your application to help CSR/SRO recruit appropriate reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight multidisciplinary aspects of the project and specific expertise types. Completing this section helps identify suitable reviewers even if other form sections are left blank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a plan for authentication of key biological and chemical resources as part of NIH Rigor and Reproducibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will comment on the suitability of the plan; if inadequate you may be asked to revise and submit an amended version via just-in-time procedures. Follow the standard NIH application instructions for this section and consult NIH 'What Kind of Information Should I Include', 'Authentication Plan Examples', and relevant NIH Policy Notices for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare biohazardous materials/activities when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists 'Biohazards' as an additional element but provides no detailed text here (placeholder). Follow applicable SF424/NOFO instructions for required content and safety documentation where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketches — who to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an NIH-format biographical sketch with research support for all principal investigators, senior/key personnel, and other significant contributors (OSCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult NIH Biosketch Format Pages and use SciENcv to format. OSCs who contribute at least one person month must be designated as senior/key personnel. Include research support information for everyone designated as senior/key personnel or OSCs (including consultants and technical staff with such designations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketches — how reviewers use them
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess whether personnel have adequate experience and whether staffing/effort are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers check that the PI and others have enough experience with the techniques to execute the Research Plan. Personal statements and 'Contributions to Science' can significantly affect the Investigator review criterion. Reviewers will check that you have requested an appropriate number of people, amount of effort, and level of expertise to conduct the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketches — creating a strong personal statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the personal statement specific to the application and explain any productivity gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the personal statement to explain how the individual’s experience qualifies them for their role. For PIs, be specific to the application; explain gaps in productivity or other issues that may affect reviewer scoring. Key personnel must explicitly state how their experience qualifies them for their project role. Carefully choose publications to highlight 'Contributions to Science' and list publications/manuscripts in press for each team member to showcase expertise. Reviewers consider seniority when evaluating contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketches — advice for new scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: If early in career or with few publications, describe contributions and training relevant to the role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have one publication, summarize its key finding briefly. If you have no publications, describe contributions to others' papers, methods used, literature reviews, or care of research animals. If no research/thesis experience, describe training to date. You do not have to be an author on publications you reference; choose a key publication that builds on your work if appropriate. Consult colleagues who serve as reviewers for further advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter — when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain circumstances require a PHS 398 cover letter; only SRO sees the cover letter (not peer reviewers or Program Officers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required reasons include approvals to submit (e.g., attach NINDS acceptance letter for grants requesting $500,000+ direct costs), conference grants (R13/U13), late applications (include reason), continuous submission (indicate if you are a study section member submitting at a nonstandard time), and indicating intent to send video files later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter — optional uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letters may be used for several optional notifications, but assignment/expertise suggestions should use PHS Assignment Request Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional uses: point out RFAs/PAs you are responding to (state the title), note special areas (human subjects, select agents), note a subaward active only some years. In the past applicants listed expertise needed to review; now use the PHS Assignment Request Form instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter — formatting and creation
rubrics_metrics.description: How to create the cover letter and which file to use in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with the title and brief description of your application. Use the PHS 398 Cover Letter File in the grant application—do not confuse it with the mandatory PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement form. Follow the format given in the SF 424 Form Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Data Management and Sharing Plan per NIH policy for applications submitted on/after Jan 25, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NINDS' dedicated Data Management and Sharing Plan page. Note that Data Sharing and Management Policy launched Jan 25, 2023, and existing resource sharing requirements remain in effect. Follow NOFO and NIH instructions for content and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Document that necessary equipment to complete the work is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe equipment availability and justify need; follow the applicable SF424 NIH instructions for content and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional facilities and other resources necessary for successful completion of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on facilities, cores, and other resources that will support the project. Follow the applicable SF424 NIH instructions for this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction to Application / Response to Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: An Introduction (for resubmission/revision) or response to prior reviews when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section is required only for resubmission or revision applications or if the NOFO specifies one. Follow the applicable SF424 NIH instructions for content and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genomic Data Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Genomic Data Sharing requirements are included under the Data Management and Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NINDS' interpretation of the NIH Genomic Data Sharing policy and follow instructions in the Data Management and Sharing Plan section and the NOFO as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support — purpose and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters of support from your institution, key personnel, collaborators, and other significant contributors to demonstrate commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should demonstrate commitment and summarize agreements in place to support the project. Familiarize with NIH SF424 Letters of Support instructions. In multi-component applications, include letters in the overall component, other components, or both unless NOFO states otherwise. You may be instructed to begin the Letters of Support attachment with a table of letter authors, institutions, and letter types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support — collaborator letters specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting a collaborator letter, provide a summary and ensure the letter states the type and availability of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide collaborators a summary of the agreement as a starting point. Letters should clearly describe the type of support (reagents, animals, human samples, technology) and indicate whether support is available to anyone on request or only to you; NIH staff consider this when assessing potential conflicts and reviewer eligibility. Do not include the formal written agreement text in the application; NIH does not request or need a copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support — avoid excessive letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit large numbers of letters of support solely as endorsements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including too many letters burdens peer reviewers and can limit the pool of eligible reviewers due to conflicts of interest; large quantities provide little added value. Include only letters described in the NOFO instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi PD/PI Leadership Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Required section for multi-PD/PI applications to explain team organization and conflict resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the team is organized, roles/responsibilities, and how conflicts will be navigated. Follow the applicable SF424 NIH instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative (public health relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Narrative limited to THREE SENTENCES describing the project's potential to improve public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the narrative succinct and focused on public health relevance; these short sections are reviewed by all and used by staff/automated systems for assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for Enhancing Diverse Perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Some NOFOs require a plan describing how diverse perspectives will be included in the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required, the NOFO will indicate this and provide instructions in Section IV. Prepare the plan only when specified by the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: References Cited / Bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite the literature to put your research in context and demonstrate field knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite current and relevant publications and interim research products (e.g., preprints) where appropriate; do not include copies of publications in the application. If a publication is public, link to it or include its NIH PubMed Central identification number. List all citations in the Other Project Information Form: Bibliography and References Cited form and follow the SF424 instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans — overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource sharing requirements remain in effect; include plans where applicable (e.g., model organisms, research tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the Data Sharing and Management Policy effective Jan 25, 2023, existing resource sharing requirements continue. Provide appropriate resource sharing plans (or justifications for not sharing) per NIH policies and NOFO instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Organism Sharing Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All NIH applications that will produce unique model organism research resources are expected to include a sharing plan or justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to extramural investigators funded by NIH grants, cooperative agreements, and contracts (including SBIR/STTR). All investigators are expected to develop a model organism sharing plan; there is no cost threshold. If producing unique model organism resources, include a plan for distribution or justify restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Tools Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether a resource generated by the project is a 'research tool' and include an appropriate sharing plan if so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the resource is primarily a tool for discovery rather than an FDA-approved product, whether it is a broad enabling invention useful to many users rather than project-specific, and whether it is readily usable/distributable as a tool. If the unique resource meets these criteria, include a resource sharing plan or justify why it cannot be shared. Review the NIH Research Tools Policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Address select agent requirements where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists 'Select Agents' but provides no expanded text here (placeholder). Follow NOFO and SF424 instructions and federal select agent regulations when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team Management Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Some application types require a Team Management Plan describing how teams will be managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow instructions provided in Section IV of the NOFO if a Team Management Plan is required for your application type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting NINDS staff / Program Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on finding and contacting Program Officers and other NINDS staff for help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit 'Find Your NINDS Program Officer' to learn how to contact Program Officers, Grants Management Specialists, Scientific Review Officers, and Health Program Specialists for assistance related to assignment, NOFO questions, and application details.
